review: 2:3–2:4 הֲיֵקַל בְּעֵינֵי אִישׁ / מוֹתוֹ וְעֵץ צְלָבוֹ — the Arabic rhetorical question (هَلْ يُسْتَخَفُّ) becomes 'would His death and the wood of His cross be light in any man's eyes'; the paraphrase was needed to keep 88.88.
3:3 עָלָיו נַפְשִׁי אַשְׁלִיךְ — echo of Ps 55:23 הַשְׁלֵךְ עַל־יְהוָה יְהָבְךָ, for عَلَيْهِ نَفْسِي أَطْرَحُ.
4:2 יוֹפִיעוּ תִּקְוָה וָגִיל — the Arabic has 'my hope and joy appear'; the Hebrew plural verb with two subjects is deliberate.
5:1 אֵין נֶחָמָה שְׁלֵמָה — 'no consolation is complete', for لَيْسَ كَمَالٌ لِلْعَزَا; the Arabic noun كَمَال is rendered as an adjective because Hebrew has no natural construct here.
6:4 פָּנִים אֶל־פָּנִים נִרְאֶה — the exact phrase of 1 Cor 13:12 in the Hebrew NT; kept whole for وَجْهًا لِوَجْهٍ سَنَرَاه.
